extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, legal bases, and imposed sanctions governing discipline of practitioners before the USPTO (misconduct definitions, relevant CFR/USC citations, procedures for suspension and reinstatement, publication and procedural obligations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and Rules of Professional Conduct prohibiting misconduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (cited: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example factual predicate: intentionally inflating the time claimed on client matters so clients were billed for time not actually spent. Such intentional overbilling constitutes dishonesty/fraud/deceit and supports disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive/unreasonable fees for legal services
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on charging excessive or unreasonable fees under the USPTO Code and Rules (cited: 37 C.F.R. § 10.36 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.105(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charging clients for time not actually expended (overbilling) can constitute unreasonable/excessive fees. The record here notes refunds to affected clients as relevant remedial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and statutory/regulatory authority for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director (and OED) have jurisdiction over practitioner discipline under federal statute and USPTO regulations (cited: 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, 11.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements resolving disciplinary action are approved by the USPTO Director pursuant to those statutes/regulations; jurisdictional citations establish the Office's authority to impose and publish discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction — suspension from practice and conditions for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may be suspended from practice before the USPTO for a specified period (here: twelve (12) months) and remain suspended until reinstated pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions may include a fixed suspension term and an ongoing suspension until a successful petition for reinstatement under the cited regulation; suspension can apply to patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters. While suspended, respondent must not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number or verified electronic system account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance obligations under §§ 11.58 and 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation for the Respondent to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and for the OED Director to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 as part of the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Final Order does not quote the text, these citations impose procedural responsibilities during and after suspension (e.g., notifying clients, filing required notices). Parties must follow the cited regulatory procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice template must state the respondent's name, registration number, the sanction imposed, the specific CFR provisions violated, the factual basis (e.g., inflated billing), and link to the OED Reading Room. Public posting is required as part of the disciplinary process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in future matters: (1) when addressing further complaints/evidence of same or similar misconduct; and (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior settlement/order can be used to aggravate future discipline or to rebut respondent assertions; prior conduct remains part of the record for future evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to seek reconsideration, review, or appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may waive rights to seek reconsideration or review under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.56 and 11.57 and waive other rights to appeal or challenge the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement may include express waivers of procedural rights to challenge the Final Order, which is a term of an agreed sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree that each party shall bear its own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost allocation (each party bears its own costs) is a standard term in settlement orders; lack of fee-shifting is a negotiated outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors: admission, cooperation, remedial steps, and lack of prior discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions of responsibility, reporting one's own misconduct to firm leadership, acceptance of responsibility, expression of regret, refunds to clients, and absence of prior discipline are relevant mitigating considerations in resolving disciplinary matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent reported the misconduct, admitted responsibility, expressed regret, and firms refunded affected clients; these facts inform the agreed sanction (e.g., settlement to suspension rather than disbarment). Investigative findings (e.g., no discernable pattern) are also factored as mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact patterns and investigative findings relevant to discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations and forensic audits (including whether a discernable pattern exists or whether audits would detect the misconduct) affect evaluation of misconduct severity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record's note that there was 'no discernable pattern' and that an audit would have been needed to discover the inflation is relevant to determining appropriate discipline and whether misconduct was systematic or isolated.
